paragraphs.source_en: On the very next day, when as usual I went out onto the veranda for a comfortable afternoon nap, my master, quite unusually, came out of his study and kept busily doing something behind me. I suddenly woke up, opened my eyes to a narrow slit, and looked to see what he was doing. It turned out he was absorbed in imitating Andrea del Sarto! At the sight, I could not help laughing; after being mocked by his friend, he had begun by taking me as his model and sketching from life. I had already had enough sleep and very much wanted to yawn. But since my master was so rarely wielding his brush with such seriousness, would it not be unkind of me to move? So I endured it as best I could and remained motionless. He had already finished the outline and was coloring in my face. I must confess that, as a cat, I am certainly not handsome. In figure, fur color, or facial features, I by no means consider myself superior to other cats. But however ugly I may be, surely I am not so strange-looking as the thing my master was now painting. To begin with, the color of the fur is wrong: mine is much like that of a Persian cat, a pale gray with yellow in it, marked with patterns like black lacquer. That is a fact no one could possibly doubt. Yet the color my master has laid on is neither yellow, nor black, nor gray, nor brown. It is a mixture of colors, impossible to say what color it is. What is especially marvelous is that the cat in the picture has no eyes at all. Of course, since he was sketching me in the posture of sound sleep, this is understandable; but as there is not even a place that looks like an eye, one cannot tell whether it is a blind cat or a sleeping cat. Inwardly I thought that, no matter how much he imitated Andrea del Sarto, nothing good could come of painting in this fashion. Still, I could not help admiring that earnest spirit of his. I wanted, if possible, to remain still as long as I could, but I had been needing to urinate for some time already. The muscles throughout my body were unbearably tense, and I had reached the point where I could not endure another minute. Having no choice, I excused myself, stretched both legs forward with all my might, lowered my head hard, and gave a great yawn. Ah! Once things had come to this, there was no point in staying meekly in place any longer. Since I had already ruined my master’s plan anyway, I might as well take the opportunity to go behind the house and relieve my small necessity. I slowly crawled away. Thereupon, in a voice mixed with disappointment and anger, my master shouted from the sitting room, “You fool!” My master has a fault: whenever he abuses someone, he invariably uses the phrase “you fool.” Since he knows no other way of cursing, one can only let him curse as he likes. My master had no understanding at all of how long I had endured for his sake, and simply kept calling me a fool; it was truly inconsiderate. Moreover, if in ordinary times, when I climbed onto his back, he would show me even a little kindness, I could bear such abuse; but when he has never done a single thing for my benefit, to call me a fool merely for going to urinate is really too much.

paragraphs.source_zh: 就在第二天，当我照例来到廊子舒舒服服睡午觉的时候，主人破例走出书斋，在我背后不停地折腾着。我突然醒来，把眼睛睁开一道细缝看看，他在干什么？原来他正在聚精会神地效法安德利亚·特尔·萨尔德呢！看到这种情景，我忍俊不禁，他受了朋友的揶揄后，首先拿我作模特儿，写起生来了。我已经睡足，非常想打个呵欠。但是想到主人难得这样认真地挥动画笔，如果我挪动身体，岂不对不起他？于是我尽量忍耐着，一动不动。他已经画好了轮廓，正在为我的面部着色。我不得不承认，作为一只猫儿，我的确算不上俊俏。无论身材、毛色，或者脸上的眉眼儿，我决不认为自己胜过其他的猫儿。但是我生得再怎么丑陋，总不至于像主人现在画出来的那副怪模怪样呀。先说毛色就不像，我的毛色很像波斯猫，淡灰中含有微黄，而且带有像黑漆一般的花纹。这是谁都不会怀疑的事实。可主人现在涂的色彩，非黄，非黑，非灰，也非褐色。那是一些颜色的混合色，无法说出是什么颜色。尤其妙的是，画中的猫竟然没有眼睛。当然，他画的是我大睡方酣时的姿态，情有可原，但是连个像眼睛的地方都看不出，根本无法判断这是瞎猫还是睡猫了。我心中暗想：不管你怎样效法安德利亚·特尔·萨尔德，这种画法肯定是画不出名堂的。但是，他那种认真的精神，不能不令我钦佩。我本想如果可能，尽量呆着不动，但是我老早就憋着一泡尿。全身筋肉紧张得难熬，已经到了一分钟也忍不了的地步。不得已，我只好对不起了，便把两腿使劲向前一伸，把头用力向下一低，打了一个大呵欠。唉！事情既然如此，再老实呆下去也毫无意义。反正主人的计划已经让我打破了，不如趁机到房后去解决我的小急吧。我慢腾腾地走开去。于是，主人发出了失望而又愤怒的声音，在客厅里大喝一声：“你这个混蛋！”我家主人有个毛病，骂人的时候总是使用“混蛋”这个字眼。除此外，他不懂得其他的骂法，所以只好随他去骂吧。主人一点不理解我为他憋了这么久的心情，一味地骂我“混蛋”，真是太不近人情啦。而且，如果平时我趴在他脊背上的时候，他能多少给我一点好颜色看，我还可以忍受这种辱骂，可是他从未做过半点对我有好处的事儿，我解小便就被骂作“混蛋”，未免太过分啦。

paragraphs.source_en: Speaking generally, human beings imagine their own strength to be something splendid, and so they are exceedingly arrogant. Unless something stronger than humans appears and chastens them, there is no telling how lawless they may become.

units.source_en: Speaking generally, human beings imagine their own strength to be something splendid, and so they are exceedingly arrogant.
units.source_zh: 说起来，人类总以为自己的力量了不起，所以狂妄自大得很。

units.source_en: Unless something stronger than humans appears and chastens them, there is no telling how lawless they may become.

units.source_zh: 如果不出现个比人更强大的东西来惩治他们，那么他们会无法无天到什么地步，那就很难逆料啦。

paragraphs.source_zh: 说起来，人类总以为自己的力量了不起，所以狂妄自大得很。如果不出现个比人更强大的东西来惩治他们，那么他们会无法无天到什么地步，那就很难逆料啦。

paragraphs.source_en: If human willfulness went only this far, it would still be bearable. But I have heard of many immoral things done by humans that are far more lamentable than this.

units.source_en: If human willfulness went only this far, it would still be bearable.
units.source_zh: 人的任性，如果只到此为止，那还可以容忍。

units.source_en: But I have heard of many immoral things done by humans that are far more lamentable than this.
units.source_zh: 但我听说人干下的许多缺德事儿，远要比这个可悲得多呢。

paragraphs.source_zh: 人的任性，如果只到此为止，那还可以容忍。但我听说人干下的许多缺德事儿，远要比这个可悲得多呢。
